title: The announced place at infinity is not constructed in this packet
body: The planning question points to cote149 scans099–101, but the supplied material for those leaves consists of earlier research notes: MPL_149_091-136_notes.md, RN099-03, locates a modular-cusp/Tate-curve proposal, and RN101-04 records “structure à l’infini”. The present packet constructs finite four-sets, squares, octahedra and Λ-modules, ending in a linear lifting problem; no cusp family, tangential point, inertia/decomposition group, or place at infinity is constructed in scans002–039. This leaves the requested cusp identification unanswered by this selection and makes no claim about the rest of cote64 or about the correctness of the earlier note’s proposed Tate calculation.
context: README.md, infinity question; MPL_149_091-136_notes.md, RN099-03 and RN101-04
ledger: Planning infinity question; no settled RESULTS_STATE entry establishes this identification; LM6 F.43 is a separate prior-run boundary claim

title: The precise advance at congruence levels2 and4
body: The concrete contribution to bridge B5 is the reduction kernel, its canonical S3-module decomposition, the associated square, and the octahedral projective quotient with its central lifting problem. LM_140-2_text.tex,568–569(68), explicitly asks for the equivariant identification sl2(F2)/F2·id≃F2^{0,1,∞}/diag, while LM_140-2_notes.md, LM_P057api R17 at569, already verifies it using A↦(v↦det(v,Av)). The formula [[a,b],[c,a]]↦[δ_(b,c)], with δ_0=0, is independently proved and checked here on all48 equivariance pairs,64 additivity pairs and8 comparisons with R17. Scans027–028 therefore add the canonical summand and its integration into the torsor model, not the first solution of R17’s already recorded calculation, and do not fix the geometric labelling0,1,∞.
ledger: Bridge B5; Hua finding 64-gl2-z4-combinatorial-model; LM2 C.d1 not re-proved

title: A finite cusp comparison worth carrying forward
body: The lower unipotent U=[[1,0],[1,1]], obtained modulo4 from LM_140-3_text.tex,§39,025(9), cycles (1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3) and fixes (0,1),(2,1), where each representative denotes its primitive-vector class modulo±1. It is therefore a quarter-turn of Δ_M, with determinant+1 and nontrivial mod-two permutation sign. This is a concrete finite test for the cusp comparison proposed by cote149 RN099-03, but the older LM passage itself says “sauf erreur” and no cusp construction follows from this computation alone. Confidence is high for the finite action because two independent enumerations agree; the geometric identification remains a proposal requiring its own source and proof.
ledger: Bridge B5 and planning infinity question; LM2 C.r1–C.r3 not thereby established

title: The all-level and arithmetic questions remain open at their recorded scope
body: No GT action on a compatible congruence tower is constructed here, so the packet does not establish the unreviewed previous-return assertion LM2 C.d1 or resolve C.d5’s simultaneous image problem. In particular, LM4_SUCCESSOR B.38’s higher-level kernel problems and E.10’s six specified congruence-kernel computations remain open in the register, and these finite calculations provide no new arithmetic image or full-GT conclusion for EXIT_TOWER E.24 or LM7_PUSH E.3. The suggested result EXIT_TOWER E.49 is explicitly unrefereed/under check in RESULTS_STATE and is not adopted as a solution; the source locators behind the LM2 §39 rows are LM_140-3_text.tex,021–030, despite the return’s LM2 label.
ledger: LM2 C.d1,C.d5; LM4_SUCCESSOR B.38,E.10; EXIT_TOWER E.24,E.49; LM7_PUSH E.3

title: S20 is not established by the projective line in these leaves
body: The object P(M) here is the projective line of a free module over the finite coefficient ring Z/4Z, with six Λ-points reducing to three F2-points. The frozen packet supplies no Gauss–Manin connection, Cartier operation, uniformization equation, or p-curvature calculation, so it cannot establish the README’s planning guess S20. The supplied catalogue SECTIONS_STATE.md,§11b and its paragraph on top-level cotes158–160, makes cotes93 and159 relevant leads, but its headings do not supply the missing differential objects or identify Grothendieck’s intention in this particular packet.
ledger: Planning S20; MPL_93_002-046 E14,E16,C29,P09 remain unadjudicated; C35 remains withdrawn

title: The supplied LM context does give a genuine analytic comparison
body: LM_140-3_text.tex,019–020, describes a complex elliptic curve by a line and a lattice and its unimodular rigidification by the upper half-plane;049–050 then discusses the analytic modular map, SL2(Z), and reduction modulo2 to a permutation group of three objects. These passages, also noted in LM_140-3_notes.md at019 R30 and050 R26–R28, give an actual genus-one setting for comparing the present finite level data. To turn that comparison into S20’s proposed differential relationship, one still needs a specified family and an identification of its relevant local system, de Rham bundle and projective connection; those are not supplied by the combinatorial equivalence alone.
ledger: Planning S20; MPL_93_002-046 P09 as a title-level lead

title: The published Gauss–Manin–Cartier relationship has precise hypotheses
scans: 002–039, whole-packet scope; literature comparison for S20
quote: S20 is a planning question, not a quotation from the manuscript
body: For a smooth proper family over a smooth complex curve, algebraic de Rham cohomology carries the Gauss–Manin connection, represented by Picard–Fuchs equations(Katz,1970,introduction). In characteristicp, Katz’s Cartier description of the conjugate spectral sequence gives zero p-curvature on its E_r-terms for r≥2 under the stated base-change or Frobenius-flatness hypotheses, hence nilpotence on de Rham cohomology; global nilpotence additionally uses the arithmetic-model and local-freeness hypotheses of Theorem10.0(Katz,1970,Theorem7.4,Corollary7.5,Theorem10.0). On a smooth characteristic-p scheme, ordinary Cartier descent concerns integrable connections with zero p-curvature, a stronger condition than nilpotence(Ogus & Vologodsky,2007,Remark2.2). These published relationships make S20 a coherent research direction but provide no documentary identification in the unavailable cote93 and159 texts.
ledger: Planning S20; MPL_93_002-046 P09; no unseen content of E14/E16/C29 inferred

title: A projective connection needs additional geometric data
body: In Hoshi’s setting of a smooth projective curve of genus at least two over an odd-characteristic base, an indigenous bundle includes a P1-bundle with connection and a Hodge section whose Kodaira–Spencer map is an isomorphism(Hoshi,2015,introduction). The rank-two formulation uses a transverse line filtration, with additional marked-point conditions in Bouw and Wewers’ formulation for hyperbolic marked curves(2006,Definition2.1), whose treatment connects such objects to second-order equations and distinguishes nilpotent from vanishing p-curvature. Hoshi’s characteristic-three results give a precise Cartier-operator comparison in that setting, but neither these modern results nor the shared word “projective” supply the connection and filtration absent from P(M) on the current pages. This is a comparison of mathematical structures, not evidence of historical dependence or of a completed S20 synthesis.
context: SECTIONS_STATE.md,cote159 headings; Bouw & Wewers(2006,§§2,3,5); Hoshi(2015,introduction and§5)
ledger: Planning S20; MPL_93_002-046 P09 remains an unprovided comparison

title: A concrete future test, without reconstructing the missing notes
body: A future comparison should obtain the actual statements behind MPL_93_002-046 E14,E16,C29,P09,C35 and the relevant cote159 leaves, then specify the base, family and characteristic of each differential object. Reduction of the present coefficient module modulo2 is not a calculation of p-curvature; for a specified characteristic-p connection, compare its linear and projective forms, fix scalar/determinant normalization and the Hodge/transverse section, then calculate ψ(D)=∇(D)^p−∇(D^[p]), with D^[p] the p-fold iterate on functions and separate zero-versus-nilpotent conclusions(Bouw & Wewers,2006,§3.1). Only after those identifications are made can the formal-deformation/coarse-invariant questions be tested, and the register’s withdrawn C35 must not be revived without its actual following explanation. Confidence is high that these distinctions are necessary, because the currently supplied finite and differential objects have different data; no claim of sufficiency or completed comparison is made.

title: Hua’s full-folder synthesis extends beyond the present evidence
body: Hua’s modernised reading of cote64,§§5–6, identifies and analyses the manuscript’s groupoid model and projective reconstruction problem, directly compared in C64-N21–N38; his project is credited for that earlier interpretation. Its later sections move to geometric octahedral configurations, Legendre pinnings, Weierstrass formulas and analytic uniformization, all outside the supplied scans002–039. These are useful follow-up leads rather than primary evidence for a cusp or differential equation in this packet; the full modernized file itself does not articulate the proposed Gauss–Manin/Cartier/p-curvature relationship. The modernized page ranges and added hypotheses are an interpretation and cannot supply missing manuscript words or an authorial page count.
context: hua_project/README.md; hua_project/64.modern.tex,scope comments,§§5–6 and later parts
